subject: Version Control Systems

assessmentTargets.concept: Identify and describe the three core areas of a Git workflow: working directory, staging area, and repository.
assessmentTargets.supportingEvidence: we have three areas. Working directory, staging area and git repository.
assessmentTargets.evidenceSpan: Segment 1 describing the Git workflow areas.
assessmentTargets.instruction: Provide a brief explanation of each area and its role in version control.

assessmentTargets.concept: Demonstrate how to stage all changes versus a single file using git add.
assessmentTargets.supportingEvidence: git add space dot, that means all the changes that you have done in your project will be saved. ... git add space a.txt ... only the changes of that particular file will be saved into the staging area.
assessmentTargets.instruction: Write the exact commands to stage (a) all files and (b) only a.txt.

assessmentTargets.concept: Create a commit with an appropriate message and explain why the message is important.
assessmentTargets.supportingEvidence: git commit will save the changes of your particular file into the repository... you have to give a message.
assessmentTargets.instruction: Compose a git commit command that includes a descriptive message.

assessmentTargets.concept: Use git diff to compare the current working state with the previous commit and interpret the output.
assessmentTargets.supportingEvidence: git diff. It will compare the changes of your current file with the previous version.
assessmentTargets.instruction: Run git diff after modifying a file and describe what the output shows.

assessmentTargets.concept: Explain how to undo staged changes using git reset and how to restore file content using git restore.
assessmentTargets.supportingEvidence: git reset. All the changes will be reverted back... git restore space dot. ... the new line also is deleted.
assessmentTargets.evidenceSpan: Segment 5 covering git reset and git restore.
assessmentTargets.instruction: Describe the sequence of commands to (a) unstage changes and (b) permanently remove an unwanted line from a file.

reserveTargets.subtopic: Initializing a Repository with git init
reserveTargets.concept: Initialize a new local Git repository and identify the hidden .git folder.
reserveTargets.supportingEvidence: git init... this particular folder which is called as sample example is converted into a git repository... there is one hidden folder called as .git.
reserveTargets.instruction: Explain what git init does and why the .git folder is hidden.

reserveTargets.subtopic: Checking Repository State with git status
reserveTargets.concept: Interpret the output of git status to determine staged, unstaged, and clean states.
reserveTargets.supportingEvidence: git status... it is telling there is one file called as a.ext in which you did not save anything... after git add dot, a.ext now is in green color... status is telling that everything is committed and you are clean.
reserveTargets.evidenceSpan: Segment 5 describing git status at various stages.
reserveTargets.instruction: List the possible colors/messages shown by git status and what they indicate.
